subject: Finding posterior covariance matrix for theta1, theta2, hopefully others

messages.author: 46d7a4fa0dad1078
messages.subject: Finding posterior covariance matrix for theta1, theta2, hopefully others
parts:
Hi there,

I am working with spatial data and I want to understand the covariance matrix related to the spatial hyperparameters: specifically, the scale parameter kappa, marginal variance of the process sigma_u^2, and also the nugget variance (which I understand to be the inverse of "The Precision of the Gaussian Observations" from mod$marginal.hyperpar. 

mod and some other code is given below, based on that from Blangiardo for the swiss rainfall example:
spde = inla.spde2.matern(mesh=mesh, alpha = 2)
formula <- rain ~ -1 + Intercept +  f(field, model=spde)
mod =   inla(formula,
             data=inla.stack.data(stack, spde=spde),
             family="gaussian",
             control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack), compute=TRUE),
             control.compute=list(cpo=TRUE, dic=TRUE),
             keep=FALSE, verbose=TRUE)
result = inla.spde2.result(mod, "field", spde)

I want to make the Gaussian assumption for these parameters, and I am using alpha=2 and d=2 (lat, lon). So it is more appropriate to use the theta1 and theta2 (which are log(tau) and log(kappa) respectively).

My question is this: Can we obtain:
the 2x2 posterior covariance matrix for (theta_1, theta_2)?
the 3x3 posterior covariance matrix for (log(eta), theta_1, theta_2), where eta is the nugget variance, that will be very good.
the 4x4 posterior covariance matrix for (log(sigma_u^2), log(eta), theta_1, theta_2), that will be great.

Thank you very much for your help!

Steve

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Finding posterior covariance matrix for theta1, theta2, hopefully others
parts:
All hyperparameters have an internal representation, for which is
used. This representation have better properties than the orgiginal
parameterisation. Like, instead of precision, we use log(precision),
etc. The documentation for each model should give this transformation.
The aim of the transformation is to make the Fisher-information matrix
about constant, so 'transforming to flatland' you might say.

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Finding posterior covariance matrix for theta1, theta2, hopefully others
parts:
The summary output displays information on the user scale (see earlier
replies about why the internal and user scale are one and the same for
spde2.matern models, with more details in the ?INLA::inla.spde2.matern
documentation.

The misc$cov.intern information is with respect to the internal theta
parameters for all models. Use inla.doc() to see documentation for
each latent and/or likelihood model of what those parameterisations
are.
For regular precision parameters, that is indeed log-precisions.

Finn
